mechanism_narrative: A sustained 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals an easing monetary cycle that compresses discount rates applied to equity cash flows, producing positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: Walk-forward Rank IC remains below 0.03 over any 2-year rolling window, or 20-day forward returns in easing periods are not significantly higher than baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 4% over two consecutive months signals weakening household income and reduced consumer spending, which depresses corporate earnings and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when UNRATE > 4% for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in personal consumption expenditures (RSAFS) exceeding 2% signals deteriorating demand, which reduces revenue growth for consumer-sensitive sectors and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when RSAFS declines > 2% over two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in industrial production (INDPRO) exceeding 1% signals supply-side weakness, which raises input costs and reduces profit margins, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when INDPRO declines > 1% over two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A 3-month rise in the federal funds rate above 4.5% signals a restrictive monetary regime that raises discount rates and depresses equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for three months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month acceleration in payroll employment growth above 0.5% signals labor market tightening and upward wage pressure, which reduces profit margins and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when PAYEMS growth > 0.5% for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A two-month decline in the Housing Starts Index (HOUST) exceeding 10% signals weakening residential investment, which reduces demand for construction-related equities and produces negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower than baseline during periods when HOUST declines > 10% over two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A joint 3-month decline in CPI inflation and a 3-month decline in the federal funds rate signals a disinflationary easing cycle, which boosts real equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS both decline for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than baseline during periods when both CPIAUCSL and FEDFUNDS decline for three months (t-test p > 0.05).
